local354.question: Among Formula 1 drivers who raced during the 1950s, which drivers completed a season in that decade with the same constructor in both the first and the last race they participated in, while also taking part in at least two distinct race rounds during that season?

candidates.sql:
WITH driver_seasons AS (
    SELECT 
        r.year,
        res.driver_id,
        MIN(r.round) as first_round,
        MAX(r.round) as last_round,
        COUNT(DISTINCT r.round) as distinct_rounds
    FROM results res
    JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
    WHERE r.year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
    GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.round) >= 2
),
constructor_first_last AS (
    SELECT 
        ds.year,
        ds.driver_id,
        ds.first_round,
        ds.last_round,
        (SELECT res2.constructor_id 
         FROM results res2 
         JOIN races r2 ON res2.race_id = r2.race_id 
         WHERE r2.year = ds.year 
           AND res2.driver_id = ds.driver_id 
           AND r2.round = ds.first_round 
         LIMIT 1) as first_constructor,
        (SELECT res2.constructor_id 
         FROM results res2 
         JOIN races r2 ON res2.race_id = r2.race_id 
         WHERE r2.year = ds.year 
           AND res2.driver_id = ds.driver_id 
           AND r2.round = ds.last_round 
         LIMIT 1) as last_constructor
    FROM driver_seasons ds
    GROUP BY ds.year, ds.driver_id, ds.first_round, ds.last_round
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    d.forename,
    d.surname
FROM constructor_first_last c
JOIN driver_seasons ds ON c.year = ds.year AND c.driver_id = ds.driver_id
JOIN drivers d ON c.driver_id = d.driver_id
WHERE c.first_constructor = c.last_constructor
ORDER BY d.surname, d.forename

candidates.sql:
WITH driver_year_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        driver_id,
        MIN(first_round) as first_round,
        MAX(last_round) as last_round,
        COUNT(*) as drive_count
    FROM drives 
    WHERE year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
    GROUP BY year, driver_id
),
first_round_constructor AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        driver_id,
        constructor_id
    FROM drives d1
    WHERE (year, driver_id) IN (
        SELECT year, driver_id FROM driver_year_stats
    )
    AND first_round = (
        SELECT first_round FROM driver_year_stats d2 
        WHERE d2.year = d1.year AND d2.driver_id = d1.driver_id 
        ORDER BY first_round 
        LIMIT 1
    )
),
last_round_constructor AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        driver_id,
        constructor_id
    FROM drives d1
    WHERE (year, driver_id) IN (
        SELECT year, driver_id FROM driver_year_stats
    )
    AND last_round = (
        SELECT last_round FROM driver_year_stats d2 
        WHERE d2.year = d1.year AND d2.driver_id = d1.driver_id 
        ORDER BY last_round DESC 
        LIMIT 1
    )
),
qualifying_seasons AS (
    SELECT 
        dy.year,
        dy.driver_id,
        dy.first_round,
        dy.last_round,
        frc.constructor_id as constructor_id
    FROM driver_year_stats dy
    JOIN first_round_constructor frc ON dy.year = frc.year AND dy.driver_id = frc.driver_id
    JOIN last_round_constructor lrc ON dy.year = lrc.year AND dy.driver_id = lrc.driver_id
    WHERE dy.first_round < dy.last_round
      AND frc.constructor_id = lrc.constructor_id
)
SELECT 
    d.forename,
    d.surname,
    d.driver_ref,
    COUNT(*) as qualifying_seasons_count
FROM qualifying_seasons qs
JOIN drivers d ON qs.driver_id = d.driver_id
GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.forename, d.surname, d.driver_ref
ORDER BY d.surname, d.forename

candidates.sql:
WITH driver_race_rounds AS (
    SELECT 
        r.year,
        res.driver_id,
        res.constructor_id,
        r.round,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.year, res.driver_id ORDER BY r.round ASC) as rn_first,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.year, res.driver_id ORDER BY r.round DESC) as rn_last
    FROM results res
    JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
    WHERE r.year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
),
driver_season_bounds AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        driver_id,
        MIN(round) as first_round,
        MAX(round) as last_round
    FROM driver_race_rounds
    GROUP BY year, driver_id
),
qualified_drivers AS (
    SELECT 
        dsb.year,
        dsb.driver_id
    FROM driver_season_bounds dsb
    JOIN driver_race_rounds dr ON dsb.year = dr.year AND dsb.driver_id = dr.driver_id AND dr.rn_first = 1
    JOIN driver_race_rounds dr2 ON dsb.year = dr2.year AND dsb.driver_id = dr2.driver_id AND dr2.rn_last = 1
    WHERE dsb.first_round < dsb.last_round
      AND dr.constructor_id = dr2.constructor_id
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    d.forename || ' ' || d.surname as driver_name
FROM qualified_drivers qd
JOIN drivers d ON qd.driver_id = d.driver_id
ORDER BY d.driver_id DESC
LIMIT 50

candidates.sql:
WITH first_drives AS (
    SELECT year, driver_id, constructor_id, first_round
    FROM drives
    WHERE year >= 1950 AND year <= 1959
      AND is_first_drive_of_season = '1'::BLOB
),
last_drives AS (
    SELECT year, driver_id, constructor_id, last_round
    FROM drives
    WHERE year >= 1950 AND year <= 1959
      AND is_final_drive_of_season = '1'::BLOB
),
qualifying_seasons AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.year, f.driver_id, f.constructor_id, f.first_round, l.last_round
    FROM first_drives f
    JOIN last_drives l ON f.year = l.year AND f.driver_id = l.driver_id
    WHERE f.constructor_id = l.constructor_id
      AND (l.last_round - f.first_round) >= 1
)
SELECT DISTINCT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname as driver_name
FROM qualifying_seasons qs
JOIN drivers d ON qs.driver_id = d.driver_id
ORDER BY d.driver_id

local356.question: Provide the full names of drivers who have been overtaken on track more times than they have overtaken others on track during race laps, excluding position changes due to pit stops (both at pit entry and exit), retirements, or position changes that occurred during the first lap of a race (considered as start movements).

candidates.sql:
WITH position_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        l1.race_id,
        l1.driver_id,
        l1.lap as change_lap,
        CASE WHEN l2.position > l1.position THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as overtaken,
        CASE WHEN l2.position < l1.position THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as overtook
    FROM lap_positions l1
    JOIN lap_positions l2 ON l1.race_id = l2.race_id AND l1.driver_id = l2.driver_id AND l1.lap + 1 = l2.lap
    WHERE l1.lap_type = 'Race' AND l2.lap_type = 'Race' AND l1.position != l2.position
    AND l1.lap > 1
)
SELECT COUNT(*) as total_changes, SUM(overtaken) as overtaken, SUM(overtook) as overtook
FROM position_changes
WHERE race_id = 841 AND driver_id = 1

candidates.sql:
WITH pit_laps AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap
    FROM pit_stops
),
lap_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        lp.race_id,
        lp.driver_id,
        lp.lap,
        lp.position,
        LAG(lp.position) OVER (PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id ORDER BY lp.lap) AS prev_position,
        LAG(lp.lap) OVER (PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id ORDER BY lp.lap) AS prev_lap,
        pl.lap AS pit_lap,
        rl.lap AS retirement_lap,
        sl.lap AS starting_lap
    FROM lap_positions lp
    LEFT JOIN pit_laps pl ON lp.race_id = pl.race_id AND lp.driver_id = pl.driver_id AND lp.lap = pl.lap
    LEFT JOIN lap_positions rl ON lp.race_id = rl.race_id AND lp.driver_id = rl.driver_id AND lp.lap = rl.lap
    LEFT JOIN lap_positions sl ON lp.race_id = sl.race_id AND lp.driver_id = sl.driver_id AND lp.lap = sl.lap
    WHERE lp.lap > 0
    AND lp.lap_type::TEXT NOT LIKE '%Retirement%'
    AND lp.lap_type::TEXT NOT LIKE '%Starting Position%'
    AND lp.position IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT race_id, lap, position, prev_position, pit_lap, prev_lap
FROM lap_changes
WHERE driver_id = 28
AND prev_position IS NOT NULL
AND (position < prev_position OR position > prev_position)  -- Only show position changes
ORDER BY race_id, lap

candidates.sql:
SELECT full_name FROM (
    WITH position_changes AS (
        SELECT 
            race_id,
            driver_id,
            lap,
            position,
            LAG(position) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, driver_id ORDER BY lap) as prev_position,
            CASE 
                WHEN position < LAG(position) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, driver_id ORDER BY lap) THEN 1  
                WHEN position > LAG(position) OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, driver_id ORDER BY lap) THEN -1 
                ELSE 0
            END as change_type
        FROM lap_positions
        WHERE lap > 0
    ),
    pit_stop_laps AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap
        FROM pit_stops
    ),
    retirement_laps AS (
        SELECT race_id, driver_id
        FROM retirements
    ),
    filtered_changes AS (
        SELECT 
            pc.race_id,
            pc.driver_id,
            pc.lap,
            pc.position,
            pc.prev_position,
            pc.change_type
        FROM position_changes pc
        WHERE pc.change_type != 0
          AND pc.lap > 1
          AND pc.driver_id NOT IN (SELECT driver_id FROM pit_stop_laps ps WHERE ps.lap = pc.lap)
          AND pc.driver_id NOT IN (SELECT driver_id FROM retirement_laps r WHERE r.race_id = pc.race_id)
    )
    SELECT dext.full_name
    FROM filtered_changes fc
    JOIN drivers_ext dext ON fc.driver_id = dext.driver_id
    GROUP BY fc.driver_id, dext.full_name
    HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN fc.change_type = -1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > SUM(CASE WHEN fc.change_type = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    ORDER BY fc.driver_id
) ORDER BY full_name

local152.question: Can you provide the top 9 directors by movie count, including their ID, name, number of movies, average inter-movie duration (rounded to the nearest integer), average rating (rounded to 2 decimals), total votes, minimum and maximum ratings, and total movie duration? Sort the output first by movie count in descending order and then by total movie duration in descending order.

candidates.sql:
WITH director_movie_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        n.name,
        COUNT(*) as movie_count,
        SUM(m.duration) as total_movie_duration,
        AVG(r.avg_rating) as avg_rating,
        SUM(r.total_votes) as total_votes,
        MIN(r.avg_rating) as min_rating,
        MAX(r.avg_rating) as max_rating
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
    GROUP BY dm.name_id, n.name
),
movie_year_with_lag AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        m.year,
        LAG(m.year) OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY m.year) as prev_year
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
),
inter_movie_duration AS (
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        AVG(year - prev_year) as avg_inter_movie_duration
    FROM movie_year_with_lag
    WHERE prev_year IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY name_id
)
SELECT 
    dms.name_id,
    dms.name,
    dms.movie_count,
    ROUND(dim.avg_inter_movie_duration) as avg_inter_movie_duration,
    ROUND(dms.avg_rating, 2) as avg_rating,
    dms.total_votes,
    dms.min_rating,
    dms.max_rating,
    dms.total_movie_duration
FROM director_movie_stats dms
JOIN inter_movie_duration dim ON dms.name_id = dim.name_id
ORDER BY dms.movie_count DESC, dms.total_movie_duration DESC
LIMIT 9

WITH director_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        n.name,
        COUNT(*) as movie_count,
        SUM(m.duration) as total_duration,
        AVG(r.avg_rating) as avg_rating,
        SUM(r.total_votes) as total_votes,
        MIN(r.avg_rating) as min_rating,
        MAX(r.avg_rating) as max_rating
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    JOIN ratings r ON dm.movie_id = r.movie_id
    GROUP BY dm.name_id, n.name
),
movie_intervals AS (
    SELECT 
        dm.name_id,
        LAG(m.year) OVER (PARTITION BY dm.name_id ORDER BY m.year, m.date_published) as prev_year,
        m.year
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
),
director_intervals AS (
    SELECT 
        name_id,
        COUNT(*) as interval_count,
        AVG(year - prev_year) as avg_inter_movie_duration
    FROM movie_intervals
    WHERE prev_year IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY name_id
)
SELECT 
    ds.name_id,
    ds.name,
    ds.movie_count,
    ROUND(dia.avg_inter_movie_duration) as avg_inter_movie_duration,
    ROUND(ds.avg_rating, 2) as avg_rating,
    ds.total_votes,
    ds.min_rating,
    ds.max_rating,
    ds.total_duration
FROM director_stats ds
JOIN director_intervals dia ON ds.name_id = dia.name_id
ORDER BY ds.movie_count DESC, ds.total_duration DESC
LIMIT 9

FROM all_pages

local331.question: Which three distinct third-page visits are most frequently observed immediately after two consecutive visits to the '/detail' page, and how many times does each third-page visit occur?

candidates.sql:
WITH ordered_visits AS (
    SELECT 
        session,
        path,
        stamp,
        LAG(path) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as prev1,
        LAG(path, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as prev2
    FROM activity_log
)
SELECT 
    path as current_path,
    COUNT(*) as occurrence_count
FROM ordered_visits
WHERE prev1 = '/detail' AND prev2 = '/detail'
GROUP BY current_path
ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC

    SELECT 
        session,
        stamp,
        path,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as visit_num

detail_pairs AS (
    SELECT 
        o1.session,

    FROM ordered_visits o1
    JOIN ordered_visits o2 ON o1.session = o2.session AND o1.visit_num = o2.visit_num + 2
    JOIN ordered_visits o3 ON o2.session = o3.session AND o2.visit_num = o3.visit_num + 1
    WHERE o1.path = '/detail' AND o2.path = '/detail'
)
SELECT third_page, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM detail_pairs GROUP BY third_page ORDER BY cnt DESC

WITH ordered_visits AS (
    SELECT 
        session,
        stamp,
        path,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as visit_num
    FROM activity_log
),
consecutive_detail AS (
    SELECT 
        session,
        stamp,
        path,
        visit_num,
        LAG(path) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as prev_path,
        LEAD(path) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as next_path
    FROM ordered_visits
)
SELECT 
    next_path,
    COUNT(*) as count
FROM consecutive_detail
WHERE prev_path = '/detail' AND path = '/detail' AND next_path IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY next_path
ORDER BY count DESC, next_path ASC
LIMIT 3

    WHEN '40s' THEN 3

Find the sessions with the minimum count of such pre-click/pre-conversion events. If multiple sessions share this minimum count, include all of them in the results. Return each qualifying session along with the corresponding path and search type.

candidates.sql:
WITH trigger_stamps AS (
    SELECT session, 
           MIN(CASE WHEN path LIKE '/detail%' OR path = '/complete' OR path LIKE '/complete%' THEN stamp END) as first_trigger_stamp
    FROM activity_log
    GROUP BY session
),
pre_trigger_counts AS (
    SELECT a.session,
           COUNT(*) as pre_trigger_count
    FROM activity_log a
    JOIN trigger_stamps t ON a.session = t.session
    WHERE t.first_trigger_stamp IS NOT NULL
      AND a.stamp < t.first_trigger_stamp
      AND a.search_type IS NOT NULL
      AND a.search_type != ''
    GROUP BY a.session
),
min_count AS (
    SELECT MIN(pre_trigger_count) as min_count
    FROM pre_trigger_counts
),
qualifying_sessions AS (
    SELECT session
    FROM pre_trigger_counts
    WHERE pre_trigger_count = (SELECT min_count FROM min_count)
)
SELECT a.session, a.path, a.search_type, a.stamp
FROM activity_log a
JOIN qualifying_sessions q ON a.session = q.session
WHERE a.stamp < (SELECT first_trigger_stamp FROM trigger_stamps t WHERE t.session = a.session)
  AND a.search_type IS NOT NULL
  AND a.search_type != ''
ORDER BY a.session, a.stamp

WITH first_detail_complete AS (
    SELECT 
        session,
        stamp,
        path,
        search_type,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) as rn
    FROM activity_log
    WHERE path = '/detail' OR path = '/detail/' OR path = '/complete'
),
first_events AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT session, stamp
    FROM first_detail_complete
    WHERE rn = 1
),
first_boundary_events AS (
    SELECT fe.session, fe.stamp, fdc.path, fdc.search_type
    FROM first_events fe
    JOIN first_detail_complete fdc ON fe.session = fdc.session AND fe.stamp = fdc.stamp AND fdc.rn = 1
),
pre_event_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        a.session,
        COUNT(*) as pre_event_count
    FROM activity_log a
    JOIN first_boundary_events fbe ON a.session = fbe.session
    WHERE a.stamp < fbe.stamp
      AND a.search_type IS NOT NULL 
      AND a.search_type != ''
    GROUP BY a.session
)
SELECT COUNT(*) as total_pre_event_sessions FROM pre_event_counts

candidates.sql:
WITH first_click AS (
    SELECT 
        session,
        MIN(stamp) as first_click_stamp
    FROM activity_log
    WHERE path IN ('/detail', '/complete')
    GROUP BY session
),
session_events AS (
    SELECT 
        a.session,
        a.stamp,
        a.path,
        a.search_type,
        fc.first_click_stamp
    FROM activity_log a
    JOIN first_click fc ON a.session = fc.session
    WHERE a.stamp < fc.first_click_stamp
),
counts AS (
    SELECT 
        session,
        COUNT(*) as pre_click_count
    FROM session_events
    WHERE search_type IS NOT NULL AND search_type != ''
    GROUP BY session
),
min_count AS (
    SELECT MIN(pre_click_count) as min_val
    FROM counts
),
qualifying_sessions AS (
    SELECT session FROM counts WHERE pre_click_count = (SELECT min_val FROM min_count)
)
SELECT 
    qs.session,
    se.path,
    se.search_type
FROM qualifying_sessions qs
JOIN session_events se ON qs.session = se.session
WHERE se.search_type IS NOT NULL AND se.search_type != ''
ORDER BY qs.session, se.stamp

WITH order_extras_total AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(extras_count) as total_extras

order_info AS (
    SELECT 
        co.order_id,
        co.pizza_id,
        CASE WHEN co.pizza_id = 1 THEN 12.0 ELSE 10.0 END as pizza_price,
        COALESCE(oe.total_extras, 0) as total_extras,
        cr.cancellation,
        pizza_price + total_extras as income
    FROM pizza_customer_orders co
    LEFT JOIN order_extras_total oe ON co.order_id = oe.order_id
    LEFT JOIN pizza_runner_orders cr ON co.order_id = cr.order_id
    WHERE cr.cancellation IS NULL OR cr.cancellation = ''
)
SELECT 
    pizza_id,
    pizza_price,
    total_extras,
    income,
    COUNT(*) as row_count
FROM order_info
WHERE pizza_id IN (1, 2)
GROUP BY pizza_id, pizza_price, total_extras, income
ORDER BY pizza_id, total_extras

local066.question: Based on our customer pizza order information, summarize the total quantity of each ingredient used in the pizzas we delivered. Output the name and quantity for each ingredient.

candidates.sql:
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT r.order_id, co.pizza_id, pr.toppings
    FROM pizza_runner_orders r 
    JOIN pizza_customer_orders co ON r.order_id = co.order_id 
    JOIN pizza_recipes pr ON co.pizza_id = pr.pizza_id
    WHERE r.cancellation IS NULL OR r.cancellation = ''
),
expanded_toppings AS (
    SELECT order_id, unnest(string_split(toppings, ', '))::INTEGER as topping_id
    FROM delivered_orders
)
SELECT pt.topping_name, COUNT(*) as quantity
FROM expanded_toppings et
JOIN pizza_toppings pt ON et.topping_id = pt.topping_id
GROUP BY pt.topping_name
ORDER BY quantity DESC, pt.topping_name

WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT r.order_id, co.pizza_id
    FROM pizza_runner_orders r
    JOIN pizza_customer_orders co ON r.order_id = co.order_id
    WHERE r.cancellation IS NULL
),
pizza_with_toppings AS (
    SELECT od.order_id, od.pizza_id, pr.toppings
    FROM delivered_orders od
    JOIN pizza_recipes pr ON od.pizza_id = pr.pizza_id
),
-- Parse recipe toppings into individual rows (using ', ' as separator)
recipe_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        pwt.order_id,
        unnest(string_to_array(pwt.toppings, ', '))::BIGINT AS topping_id
    FROM pizza_with_toppings pwt
),
-- Parse exclusions into individual rows (using ',' as separator, only for orders with exclusions)
order_exclusions AS (
    SELECT 
        co.order_id,
        unnest(string_to_array(co.exclusions, ','))::BIGINT AS excluded_top_id
    FROM pizza_customer_orders co
    WHERE co.order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM delivered_orders)
       AND co.exclusions IS NOT NULL
       AND co.exclusions != ''
),
-- Get final toppings (recipe toppings minus exclusions)
final_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        rt.order_id,
        rt.topping_id
    FROM recipe_toppings rt
    LEFT JOIN order_exclusions oe ON rt.order_id = oe.order_id AND rt.topping_id = oe.excluded_top_id
    WHERE oe.excluded_top_id IS NULL
)
SELECT pt.topping_name, COUNT(*) AS quantity
FROM final_toppings ft
JOIN pizza_toppings pt ON ft.topping_id = pt.topping_id
GROUP BY pt.topping_name
ORDER BY quantity DESC, pt.topping_name

local073.question: For each pizza order, provide a single result row with the row ID, order ID, customer ID, pizza name, and final set of ingredients. The final ingredients are determined by starting with the standard toppings from the pizza’s recipe, removing any excluded toppings, and adding any extra toppings. Present the ingredients in a string starting with the pizza name followed by ': ', with ingredients listed in alphabetical order. Ingredients appearing multiple times (e.g., from standard and extra toppings) should be prefixed with '2x' and listed first, followed by single-occurrence ingredients, both in alphabetical order. Group by row ID, order ID, pizza name, and order time to ensure each order appears once. Sort results by row ID in ascending order. Assign pizza_id 1 to 'Meatlovers' pizzas and pizza_id 2 to all others.

candidates.sql:
WITH 
standard_toppings AS (
    SELECT pizza_id, 
           SPLIT(REPLACE(toppings, ', ', ','), ',') as topping_list
    FROM pizza_recipes
),
expanded_standard AS (
    SELECT pizza_id, topping_id
    FROM standard_toppings, unnest(topping_list) as t(topping_id)
),
orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, customer_id, pizza_id, exclusions, extras, order_time 
    FROM pizza_customer_orders
),
exclusions_array AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           SPLIT(REPLACE(TRIM(COALESCE(exclusions, '')), ', ', ','), ',') as excl_list
    FROM orders
),
extras_array AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           SPLIT(REPLACE(TRIM(COALESCE(extras, '')), ', ', ','), ',') as extra_list
    FROM orders
),
test AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.pizza_id, o.exclusions, o.extras,
           ea.excl_list, ex.extra_list,
           ea.excl_list @> ARRAY[4::VARCHAR] as has_4_in_excl,
           ex.extra_list @> ARRAY[4::VARCHAR] as has_4_in_extra
    FROM orders o
    LEFT JOIN exclusions_array ea ON o.order_id = ea.order_id
    LEFT JOIN extras_array ex ON o.order_id = ex.order_id
    WHERE o.order_id = 9
)
SELECT * FROM test

WITH 
orders AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.pizza_id,
        o.exclusions,
        o.extras,
        o.order_time,
        n.pizza_name,
        unnest(string_to_array(REPLACE(p.toppings, ' ', ''), ',')) AS standard_topping_id
    FROM pizza_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_names n ON o.pizza_id = n.pizza_id
    JOIN pizza_recipes p ON o.pizza_id = p.pizza_id
),
exclusions_set AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        unnest(string_to_array(REPLACE(exclusions, ' ', ''), ',')) AS topping_id
    FROM pizza_customer_orders
    WHERE exclusions IS NOT NULL AND exclusions != ''
),
extras_set AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.pizza_id,
        n.pizza_name,
        o.order_time,
        unnest(string_to_array(REPLACE(o.extras, ' ', ''), ',')) AS topping_id
    FROM pizza_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_names n ON o.pizza_id = n.pizza_id
    WHERE o.extras IS NOT NULL AND o.extras != ''
),
final_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        o.pizza_id,
        o.pizza_name,
        o.order_time,
        o.standard_topping_id AS topping_id
    FROM orders o
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM exclusions_set e 
        WHERE e.order_id = o.order_id AND e.topping_id = o.standard_topping_id
    )
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        es.order_id,
        es.customer_id,
        es.pizza_id,
        es.pizza_name,
        es.order_time,
        es.topping_id AS topping_id
    FROM extras_set es
),
counted_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        pizza_id,
        pizza_name,
        order_time,
        topping_id,
        COUNT(*) AS count
    FROM final_toppings
    GROUP BY order_id, customer_id, pizza_id, pizza_name, order_time, topping_id
),
-- Join with pizza_toppings to get names
titled_toppings AS (
    SELECT 
        ct.order_id,
        ct.customer_id,
        ct.pizza_id,
        ct.pizza_name,
        ct.order_time,
        ct.topping_id,
        ct.count,
        t.topping_name
    FROM counted_toppings ct
    JOIN pizza_toppings t ON ct.topping_id = t.topping_id
)

candidates.sql:
WITH candidate_words AS (
    SELECT words, LENGTH(words) as len, SUBSTR(words, 1, 1) as first_char
    FROM word_list
    WHERE LENGTH(words) BETWEEN 4 AND 5
    AND SUBSTR(words, 1, 1) = 'r'
),
word_chars AS (
    SELECT words, len, first_char, SUBSTR(words, 1, 1) as ch FROM candidate_words
    UNION ALL
    SELECT words, len, first_char, SUBSTR(words, 2, 1) as ch FROM candidate_words
    UNION ALL
    SELECT words, len, first_char, SUBSTR(words, 3, 1) as ch FROM candidate_words
    UNION ALL
    SELECT words, len, first_char, SUBSTR(words, 4, 1) as ch FROM candidate_words
    UNION ALL
    SELECT words, len, first_char, SUBSTR(words, 5, 1) as ch FROM candidate_words
),
words_with_signature AS (
    SELECT 
        words,
        len,
        first_char,
        STRING_AGG(ch, '' ORDER BY ch) as sorted_letters
    FROM word_chars
    GROUP BY words, len, first_char
),
signature_groups AS (
    SELECT 
        sorted_letters,
        COUNT(*) as word_count
    FROM words_with_signature
    GROUP BY sorted_letters
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
SELECT 
    w.words,
    (s.word_count - 1) as anagram_count
FROM words_with_signature w
JOIN signature_groups s ON w.sorted_letters = s.sorted_letters
ORDER BY w.words
LIMIT 20

candidates.sql:
WITH word_letters AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        words,
        LENGTH(words) as len,
        pos,
        SUBSTR(words, pos, 1) as letter
    FROM word_list
    CROSS JOIN UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(1, LENGTH(words))) as t(pos)
),
letter_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        words,
        len,
        SUM(CASE WHEN letter = 'a' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cnt_a,
        SUM(CASE WHEN letter = 'b' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cnt_b,
        SUM(CASE WHEN letter = 'c' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cnt_c,
        SUM(CASE WHEN letter = 'd' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cnt_d
    FROM word_letters
    GROUP BY words, len
),
word_sigs AS (
    SELECT 
        words,
        len,
        cnt_a || cnt_b || cnt_c || cnt_d as partial_sig
    FROM letter_counts
    WHERE len IN (4, 5)
    AND SUBSTR(words, 1, 1) = 'r'
    AND cnt_a = 2 AND cnt_d = 1
)
SELECT words, len, partial_sig FROM word_sigs ORDER BY words

local244.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
local244.doc:
# Music Length Types

## Short 
- Duration between the minimum value and the midpoint between the minimum and average values.

## Medium 
- Duration between the midpoint between the minimum and average values and the midpoint between the average and maximum values.

## Long 
- Duration between the midpoint between the average and maximum values and the maximum value.

candidates.sql:
WITH stats AS (
    SELECT 
        MIN(Milliseconds) as min_ms,
        AVG(Milliseconds) as avg_ms,
        MAX(Milliseconds) as max_ms
    FROM Track
),
midpoints AS (
    SELECT 
        (min_ms + avg_ms) / 2.0 as mid1,
        (avg_ms + max_ms) / 2.0 as mid2
    FROM stats
)
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN t.Milliseconds <= m.mid1 THEN 'short'
        WHEN t.Milliseconds > m.mid1 AND t.Milliseconds <= m.mid2 THEN 'medium'
        WHEN t.Milliseconds > m.mid2 THEN 'long'
    END as category,
    MIN(t.Milliseconds / 60000.0) as min_duration_minutes,
    MAX(t.Milliseconds / 60000.0) as max_duration_minutes,
    SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) as total_revenue
FROM Track t
CROSS JOIN midpoints m
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category

reasoning.summary: Track duration classification with minimum, maximum duration in minutes and total revenue grouped by category (short, medium, long)

WITH track_stats AS (
    SELECT MIN(Milliseconds) as min_ms, AVG(Milliseconds) as avg_ms, MAX(Milliseconds) as max_ms FROM Track
),
thresholds AS (
    SELECT 
        min_ms,
        avg_ms,
        max_ms,
        (min_ms + avg_ms) / 2.0 as short_upper,
        (avg_ms + max_ms) / 2.0 as medium_upper
    FROM track_stats
),
track_with_category AS (
    SELECT 
        t.TrackId,
        t.Name,
        t.Milliseconds,
        t.UnitPrice,
        il.Quantity,
        (t.Milliseconds * 1.0 / 1000.0) as duration_minutes,
        (t.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) as revenue,
        CASE 
            WHEN t.Milliseconds <= th.short_upper THEN 'Short'
            WHEN t.Milliseconds <= th.medium_upper THEN 'Medium'
            ELSE 'Long'
        END as category
    FROM Track t
    JOIN thresholds th ON 1=1
    JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
)
SELECT 
    category,
    MIN(duration_minutes) as min_duration_minutes,
    MAX(duration_minutes) as max_duration_minutes,
    SUM(revenue) as total_revenue
FROM track_with_category
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY 
    CASE category 
        WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 
        WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 
        WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 
    END

),

        SUM(total_qty) AS total_leaf_qty
    FROM leaf_level

)

FROM total_by_root

candidates.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy AS (
    SELECT 
        packaging_id as root_id,
        contains_id as current_id,
        qty as current_qty,
        1 as depth,
        qty as cumulative_qty
    FROM packaging_relations
    WHERE packaging_id IN (531, 532, 533, 534)
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        h.root_id,
        pr.contains_id as current_id,
        pr.qty as current_qty,
        h.depth + 1,
        h.cumulative_qty * pr.qty
    FROM hierarchy h
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON h.current_id = pr.packaging_id
)
SELECT 
    p_root.id as root_id,
    p_root.name as container_name,
    p_curr.id as current_id,
    p_curr.name as item_name,
    SUM(h.cumulative_qty) as total_accumulated_qty
FROM hierarchy h
JOIN packaging p_root ON h.root_id = p_root.id
JOIN packaging p_curr ON h.current_id = p_curr.id
GROUP BY p_root.id, p_root.name, p_curr.id, p_curr.name
HAVING SUM(h.cumulative_qty) > 500
ORDER BY p_root.id, p_curr.id

local272.question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.

candidates.sql:
WITH order_lines_cte AS (
    SELECT product_id, qty as order_qty, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY product_id, qty) as rn
    FROM orderlines
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
inventory_sorted AS (
    SELECT 
        i.product_id,
        i.location_id,
        l.aisle,
        l.position,
        i.purchase_id,
        i.qty,
        p.purchased,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty ASC) as rn
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE i.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_lines_cte)
    AND l.warehouse = 1
),
order_total AS (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(order_qty) as total_order_qty
    FROM order_lines_cte
    GROUP BY product_id
),
picking AS (
    SELECT 
        inv.product_id,
        inv.location_id,
        inv.aisle,
        inv.position,
        inv.qty as avail_qty,
        inv.rn,
        ot.total_order_qty,
        CASE 
            WHEN COALESCE(ot.total_order_qty - SUM(inv.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY inv.product_id ORDER BY inv.rn ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), ot.total_order_qty) > 0 
            THEN LEAST(inv.qty, COALESCE(ot.total_order_qty - SUM(inv.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY inv.product_id ORDER BY inv.rn ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), ot.total_order_qty))
            ELSE 0 
        END as pick_qty
    FROM inventory_sorted inv
    JOIN order_total ot ON inv.product_id = ot.product_id
)
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, pick_qty 
FROM picking 
WHERE pick_qty > 0 
ORDER BY product_id, rn

SELECT 
    product_id,
    SUM(pick_qty) as total_picked
FROM (
    WITH order_lines AS (
        SELECT 
            id,
            order_id,
            product_id,
            qty,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) as line_seq,
            SUM(qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id) as product_cumulative_qty
        FROM orderlines
        WHERE order_id = 423
    ),
    product_totals AS (
        SELECT 
            product_id,
            MAX(product_cumulative_qty) as total_needed
        FROM order_lines
        GROUP BY product_id
    ),
    inv_sorted AS (
        SELECT 
            i.product_id,
            i.location_id,
            l.aisle,
            l.position,
            i.qty as available_qty,
            p.purchased,
            i.purchase_id,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty) as inv_seq
        FROM inventory i
        JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
        JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
        WHERE l.warehouse = 1
          AND i.product_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM orderlines WHERE order_id = 423)
    ),
    with_cumulative AS (
        SELECT 
            pt.product_id,
            i.location_id,
            i.aisle,
            i.position,
            i.available_qty,
            i.inv_seq,
            i.purchased,
            pt.total_needed,
            SUM(i.available_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY pt.product_id ORDER BY i.inv_seq) as cumulative_available
        FROM product_totals pt
        JOIN inv_sorted i ON pt.product_id = i.product_id
    ),
    with_pick_qty AS (
        SELECT 
            product_id,
            location_id,
            aisle,
            position,
            available_qty,
            inv_seq,
            purchased,
            total_needed,
            cumulative_available,
            LEAST(available_qty, total_needed - COALESCE(LAG(cumulative_available) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY inv_seq), 0)) as calc_pick_qty
        FROM with_cumulative
    ),
    final_pick AS (
        SELECT 
            product_id,
            aisle,
            position,
            calc_pick_qty as pick_qty
        FROM with_pick_qty
        WHERE calc_pick_qty > 0
    )
    SELECT * FROM final_pick
) t

WITH RECURSIVE order_lines AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, qty as order_qty,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS line_seq
    FROM orderlines 
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
product_inventory AS (
    SELECT ol.product_id, ol.order_qty,
           i.location_id, i.qty AS inv_qty, i.purchase_id,
           l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position, p.purchased,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY ol.product_id 
               ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty
           ) AS rn
    FROM order_lines ol
    JOIN inventory i ON ol.product_id = i.product_id
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY rn) as rn_num
    FROM product_inventory
),
rec_calc(product_id, rn_num, inv_qty, aisle, position, location_id, purchased, rn, order_qty, prev_pick_total, pick_qty) AS (
    SELECT r.product_id, r.rn_num, r.inv_qty, r.aisle, r.position, r.location_id, r.purchased, r.rn, r.order_qty, 0, LEAST(r.inv_qty, r.order_qty)
    FROM ranked r
    WHERE r.rn_num = 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT r.product_id, r.rn_num, r.inv_qty, r.aisle, r.position, r.location_id, r.purchased, r.rn, r.order_qty, 
           COALESCE(prev_pick_total + pick_qty, 0),
           LEAST(r.inv_qty, COALESCE(r.order_qty - (prev_pick_total + pick_qty), 0))
    FROM ranked r
    JOIN rec_calc rc ON r.product_id = rc.product_id AND r.rn_num = rc.rn_num + 1
)
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, location_id, pick_qty
FROM rec_calc
WHERE product_id IN (4280, 6520) AND pick_qty > 0
ORDER BY product_id, rn_num

WITH order_qty AS (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(qty) as total_qty
    FROM orderlines
    WHERE order_id = 423
    GROUP BY product_id
),
inventory_with_order AS (
    SELECT 
        i.id as inv_id,
        i.location_id,
        i.product_id,
        i.purchase_id,
        i.qty as inv_qty,
        l.aisle,
        l.position,
        p.purchased,
        o.total_qty as order_qty_needed,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty) as rn,
        SUM(i.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as cum_inv_qty
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    JOIN order_qty o ON i.product_id = o.product_id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
),
with_prev AS (
    SELECT 
        *,
        LAG(cum_inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY rn) as prev_cum_inv_qty
    FROM inventory_with_order
),
picked AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        aisle,
        position,
        CASE 
            WHEN prev_cum_inv_qty IS NULL OR prev_cum_inv_qty < order_qty_needed
            THEN LEAST(inv_qty, order_qty_needed - prev_cum_inv_qty)
            ELSE 0
        END as picked_qty
    FROM with_prev
)
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, picked_qty
FROM picked
WHERE picked_qty > 0
ORDER BY product_id, aisle, position

WITH inventory_fifo AS (
    SELECT 
        i.product_id,
        i.location_id,
        p.purchased,
        i.qty as available_qty,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty ASC) as fifo_rank
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
)
SELECT * FROM inventory_fifo
WHERE product_id = 4280
ORDER BY fifo_rank

candidates.sql:
WITH ordered_inventory AS (
    SELECT ol.order_id, ol.product_id, ol.qty as required_qty,
           o.ordered as order_date,
           i.location_id, i.purchase_id, p.purchased, i.qty as inv_qty,
           i.qty as inv_available,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY ol.order_id, ol.product_id 
               ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty
           ) as inv_rn
    FROM orderlines ol
    JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
    JOIN inventory i ON ol.product_id = i.product_id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE ol.product_id = 5310
),
with_cumulative AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, required_qty, order_date, inv_available, inv_rn,
           SUM(inv_available) OVER (
               PARTITION BY order_id, product_id 
               ORDER BY inv_rn
               ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
           ) as cum_inv
    FROM ordered_inventory
),
with_prev_cum AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, required_qty, order_date, inv_available, inv_rn, cum_inv,
           COALESCE(LAG(cum_inv) OVER (PARTITION BY order_id, product_id ORDER BY inv_rn), 0) as prev_cum_inv
    FROM with_cumulative
),
-- Calculate the total required for this product
product_totals AS (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(required_qty) as total_required
    FROM ordered_inventory
    GROUP BY product_id
),
with_total_required AS (
    SELECT oi.order_id, oi.product_id, oi.required_qty, oi.order_date, oi.inv_available, oi.inv_rn,
           wc.cum_inv, wc.prev_cum_inv, pt.total_required
    FROM ordered_inventory oi
    JOIN with_prev_cum wc ON oi.order_id = wc.order_id AND oi.product_id = wc.product_id AND oi.inv_rn = wc.inv_rn
    JOIN product_totals pt ON oi.product_id = pt.product_id
),
-- Calculate cumulative allocated
with_cumulative_allocated AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, required_qty, order_date, inv_available, inv_rn, cum_inv, prev_cum_inv, total_required,
           -- The cumulative allocated after this item is min(total_required, cum_inv)
           LEAST(CAST(total_required AS DOUBLE), cum_inv) as cum_allocated,
           LEAST(CAST(total_required AS DOUBLE), prev_cum_inv) as prev_allocated
    FROM with_total_required
)
SELECT inv_rn, required_qty, inv_available, cum_inv, prev_cum_inv, total_required,
       cum_allocated, prev_allocated,
       cum_allocated - prev_allocated as allocated_qty
FROM with_cumulative_allocated
ORDER BY inv_rn

# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

WITH monthly_totals AS (
    SELECT ms.product_id, mth, qty,
           (CAST(SUBSTR(mth, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - 2016) * 12 + (CAST(SUBSTR(mth, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) - 1) + 1 as month_num
    FROM monthly_sales ms
),
window_sums AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, qty, month_num,
           SUM(qty) OVER (
               PARTITION BY product_id 
               ORDER BY month_num 
               ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 6 FOLLOWING
           ) as window1_sum,
           SUM(qty) OVER (
               PARTITION BY product_id 
               ORDER BY month_num 
               ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 5 FOLLOWING
           ) as window2_sum
    FROM monthly_totals
),
cma_calc AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, month_num, qty,
           (window1_sum + window2_sum) / 24.0 as cma,
           qty / ((window1_sum + window2_sum) / 24.0) as ratio
    FROM window_sums
    WHERE month_num >= 7 AND month_num <= 30
)
SELECT product_id, 
       COUNT(*) as total_months_2017,
       MIN(ratio) as min_ratio,
       MAX(ratio) as max_ratio
FROM cma_calc
WHERE month_num >= 13 AND month_num <= 24
GROUP BY product_id
HAVING MIN(ratio) >= 2
ORDER BY product_id

WITH monthly_data AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        CAST(mth AS DATE) as month_date,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CAST(mth AS DATE)) as month_num,
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(mth AS DATE)) as year,
        qty
    FROM monthly_sales
),
with_windows AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        month_date,
        month_num,
        year,
        qty,
        SUM(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id 
            ORDER BY month_date 
            RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '5' MONTH PRECEDING AND INTERVAL '6' MONTH FOLLOWING
        ) as window1_sum,
        SUM(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id 
            ORDER BY month_date 
            RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '6' MONTH PRECEDING AND INTERVAL '5' MONTH FOLLOWING
        ) as window2_sum
    FROM monthly_data
),
with_cma AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        month_date,
        month_num,
        year,
        qty,
        (window1_sum + window2_sum) / 24.0 as cma,
        qty / ((window1_sum + window2_sum) / 24.0) as ratio
    FROM with_windows
),
yearly_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        MIN(ratio) as min_ratio,
        MAX(ratio) as max_ratio,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN ratio > 2 THEN 1 END) as months_above_2
    FROM with_cma
    WHERE year = 2017
    GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT product_id, min_ratio, max_ratio, months_above_2
FROM yearly_stats
WHERE months_above_2 = 12
ORDER BY product_id

candidates.sql:
WITH month_data AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, qty FROM monthly_sales
),
target_months AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT mth FROM month_data WHERE mth::DATE >= '2017-01-01' AND mth::DATE <= '2017-12-31'
),
window_sums AS (
    SELECT 
        t.mth as target_mth,
        (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(md.qty), 0)
         FROM month_data md
         WHERE md.mth::DATE >= t.mth::DATE - (INTERVAL '5 MONTHS')
           AND md.mth::DATE <= t.mth::DATE + (INTERVAL '6 MONTHS')
           AND md.mth::DATE != t.mth::DATE
        ) as window1_sum,
        (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(md.qty), 0)
         FROM month_data md
         WHERE md.mth::DATE >= t.mth::DATE - (INTERVAL '6 MONTHS')
           AND md.mth::DATE <= t.mth::DATE + (INTERVAL '5 MONTHS')
           AND md.mth::DATE != t.mth::DATE
        ) as window2_sum
    FROM target_months t
)
SELECT * FROM window_sums

local277.question: What is the average forecasted annual sales for products 4160 and 7790 during 2018, using monthly sales data starting from January 2016 for the first 36 months, applying seasonality adjustments from time steps 7 through 30, and employing a weighted regression method to estimate sales?
local277.doc:
# Explanation of Metrics

## 1. Sales-to-CMA Ratio
- **Definition**: This ratio compares actual sales to the centered moving average (CMA) of sales.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Centered Moving Average (CMA)**: The CMA is a smoothed value of sales calculated over a rolling 12-month period. It averages sales from the months before and after a given month, specifically using two overlapping windows (5 months before and 6 months after, and vice versa).
  - **Sales-to-CMA Ratio**: The ratio is computed by dividing the actual sales amount for a month by its corresponding CMA value. A ratio greater than 2 indicates that the actual sales are more than twice the smoothed average for that period, suggesting significantly higher-than-average sales.

## 2. 12-Month Overlapping Windows
- **Definition**: A method to smooth sales data over time by averaging values in a specified window.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Window Size**: The window spans 12 months, with the specific approach involving overlapping periods. 
  - **First Window**: For a given month, this window includes 5 months before and 6 months after.
  - **Second Window**: Another window includes 6 months before and 5 months after the given month.
  - **Averaging**: Sales data is averaged over these two overlapping windows to compute the CMA. This method smooths out fluctuations by considering both the past and future sales in the calculation.

## 3. Restriction to the 7th and 30th Months
- **Definition**: A filter applied to focus calculations within a specific range of months.
- **Calculation**:
  - **Time Range**: Only the months between the 7th and 30th time steps (which correspond to specific periods) are considered for calculating the CMA and ratio.
  - **Purpose**: This restriction is used to avoid edge effects in the data where the moving average might be less reliable (e.g., at the very beginning or end of the available data). By focusing on these months, the calculations are more stable and meaningful.

candidates.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        (CAST(SUBSTRING(mth, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - 2016) * 12 + CAST(SUBSTRING(mth, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) AS ts
    FROM monthly_sales
    WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)
)
SELECT 
    product_id,
    ts,
    qty AS actual_2018
FROM base_data
WHERE ts >= 25 AND ts <= 36
ORDER BY product_id, ts

    SELECT product_id, 
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY mth) as rn,
           qty
    FROM monthly_sales 
    WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)

FROM ranked_data 
WHERE rn BETWEEN 7 AND 30
GROUP BY product_id

WITH base AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    TRY_CAST(mth AS DATE) as month_date,
    qty,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY TRY_CAST(mth AS DATE)) as time_step,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TRY_CAST(mth AS DATE)) as month_of_year
  FROM monthly_sales
  WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)
),
params AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    time_step,
    qty,
    month_of_year
  FROM base
),
seasonal_factors AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    month_of_year,
    AVG(qty) as seasonal_factor
  FROM params
  WHERE time_step BETWEEN 7 AND 30
  GROUP BY product_id, month_of_year
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(seasonal_factor) as avg_val FROM seasonal_factors
),
seasonal_indices AS (
  SELECT 
    sf.product_id,
    sf.month_of_year,
    sf.seasonal_factor / o.avg_val as seasonal_index
  FROM seasonal_factors sf
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg o
),
means AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    AVG(time_step * qty) / AVG(time_step) as y_bar_w,
    AVG(time_step * time_step) / AVG(time_step) as x_bar_w
  FROM params
  GROUP BY product_id
),
slope AS (
  SELECT 
    p.product_id,
    SUM(p.time_step * (p.time_step - m.x_bar_w) * (p.qty - m.y_bar_w)) / SUM(p.time_step * (p.time_step - m.x_bar_w) * (p.time_step - m.x_bar_w)) as slope
  FROM params p
  JOIN means m ON p.product_id = m.product_id
  GROUP BY p.product_id
),
forecast AS (
  SELECT 
    p.product_id,
    p.time_step,
    p.month_of_year,
    s.slope,
    m.y_bar_w - s.slope * m.x_bar_w as intercept,
    (m.y_bar_w - s.slope * m.x_bar_w) + s.slope * p.time_step as trend_forecast,
    si.seasonal_index
  FROM params p
  JOIN slope s ON p.product_id = s.product_id
  JOIN means m ON p.product_id = m.product_id
  JOIN seasonal_indices si ON p.product_id = si.product_id AND p.month_of_year = si.month_of_year
  WHERE p.time_step >= 25 AND p.time_step <= 36
)
SELECT 
  product_id,
  time_step,
  month_of_year,
  trend_forecast,
  seasonal_index,
  trend_forecast * seasonal_index as adjusted_forecast
FROM forecast
ORDER BY product_id, time_step

WITH monthly_data AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    mth,
    TRY_CAST(mth AS DATE) as parsed_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY mth) as time_step,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM TRY_CAST(mth AS DATE)) as month_of_year,
    qty
  FROM monthly_sales 
  WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)
),
seasonality_calc AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    month_of_year,
    AVG(qty) as avg_qty_for_month
  FROM monthly_data
  WHERE time_step BETWEEN 7 AND 30
  GROUP BY product_id, month_of_year
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT product_id, AVG(avg_qty_for_month) as overall_avg FROM seasonality_calc GROUP BY product_id
),
seasonality_factors AS (
  SELECT 
    ma.product_id,
    ma.month_of_year,
    ma.avg_qty_for_month / oa.overall_avg as seasonality_factor
  FROM seasonality_calc ma
  JOIN overall_avg oa ON ma.product_id = oa.product_id
),
weighted_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    SUM(time_step) as sum_w,
    SUM(time_step * time_step) as sum_wx2,
    SUM(time_step * qty) as sum_wy,
    SUM(time_step * time_step * qty) as sum_wxy
  FROM monthly_data
  GROUP BY product_id
),
regression AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    sum_wx2 / sum_w as weighted_mean_x,
    sum_wy / sum_w as weighted_mean_y,
    (sum_wxy - sum_w * (sum_wx2 / sum_w) * (sum_wy / sum_w)) / 
    (sum_wx2 - sum_w * (sum_wx2 / sum_w) * (sum_wx2 / sum_w)) as weighted_slope,
    weighted_mean_y - weighted_slope * weighted_mean_x as weighted_intercept
  FROM weighted_stats
),
forecast AS (
  SELECT 
    r.product_id,
    md.time_step,
    md.month_of_year,
    r.weighted_slope * md.time_step + r.weighted_intercept as forecasted_sales
  FROM regression r
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT product_id, time_step, month_of_year FROM monthly_data 
    WHERE time_step BETWEEN 25 AND 36
  ) md
  WHERE r.product_id = md.product_id
),
adjusted_forecast AS (
  SELECT 
    f.product_id,
    f.time_step,
    f.month_of_year,
    f.forecasted_sales * sf.seasonality_factor as adjusted_forecast
  FROM forecast f
  JOIN seasonality_factors sf ON f.product_id = sf.product_id AND f.month_of_year = sf.month_of_year
),
annual_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id,
    SUM(adjusted_forecast) as forecasted_annual_sales
  FROM adjusted_forecast
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT 
  product_id,
  forecasted_annual_sales,
  ROUND(forecasted_annual_sales, 2) as forecasted_annual_sales_rounded
FROM annual_sales
ORDER BY product_id

local279.question: Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December 2018 inventory levels, where we restock a product if its ending inventory drops below the minimum required level, determine for each product the month in 2019 where the absolute difference between its ending inventory and the minimum required level is the smallest, and return the product_id, that month, and the absolute difference.

candidates.sql:
WITH monthly_abs_diff AS (
  SELECT mb.product_id, mb.mth, mb.qty, pm.qty_minimum, ABS(mb.qty - pm.qty_minimum) as abs_diff 
  FROM monthly_budget mb
  JOIN product_minimums pm ON mb.product_id = pm.product_id
  WHERE mb.mth >= '2019-01-01' AND mb.mth < '2020-01-01'
),
min_diff_per_product AS (
  SELECT product_id, MIN(abs_diff) as min_abs_diff
  FROM monthly_abs_diff
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT mad.product_id, mad.mth, mad.qty, mad.qty_minimum, mad.abs_diff
FROM monthly_abs_diff mad
JOIN min_diff_per_product mdp ON mad.product_id = mdp.product_id AND mad.abs_diff = mdp.min_abs_diff
ORDER BY mad.product_id, mad.mth

candidates.sql:
SELECT 
    im.product_id,
    '2019-01-01' as month,
    ABS(im.total_inventory - pm.qty_minimum) as abs_diff
FROM (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(qty) as total_inventory 
    FROM inventory 
    WHERE product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM product_minimums)
    GROUP BY product_id
) im
JOIN product_minimums pm ON im.product_id = pm.product_id
ORDER BY im.product_id

local130.question: Could you provide a list of last names for all students who have completed English courses (where completion is defined as having a ClassStatus of 2), along with their quintile ranks based on their individual grades in those courses? The quintile should be determined by calculating how many students have grades greater than or equal to each student's grade, then dividing this ranking by the total number of students who completed English courses. The quintiles should be labeled as "First" (top 20%), "Second" (top 21-40%), "Third" (top 41-60%), "Fourth" (top 61-80%), and "Fifth" (bottom 20%). Please sort the results from highest performing quintile to lowest (First to Fifth).

candidates.sql:
WITH english_students AS (
    SELECT 
        ss.StudentID,
        stud.StudLastName,
        ss.Grade
    FROM Student_Schedules ss
    JOIN Classes c ON ss.ClassID = c.ClassID
    JOIN Subjects sub ON c.SubjectID = sub.SubjectID
    JOIN Students stud ON ss.StudentID = stud.StudentID
    WHERE ss.ClassStatus = 2 
    AND (sub.SubjectName LIKE '%English%' OR sub.SubjectName LIKE '%Composition%')
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        StudentID,
        StudLastName,
        Grade,
        COUNT(*) OVER () as total_students,
        SUM(1) OVER (ORDER BY Grade DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as count_ge
    FROM english_students
)
SELECT 
    StudLastName,
    CASE 
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.2 THEN 'First'
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.4 THEN 'Second'
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.6 THEN 'Third'
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.8 THEN 'Fourth'
        ELSE 'Fifth'
    END as quintile
FROM ranked
ORDER BY CASE 
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.2 THEN 1
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.4 THEN 2
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.6 THEN 3
        WHEN count_ge * 1.0 / total_students <= 0.8 THEN 4
        ELSE 5
    END,
    Grade DESC

WITH customer_first_payments AS (

WITH customer_ltv AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           MIN(payment_date) as initial_purchase_date,

customer_7day AS (

           cl.initial_purchase_date,
           cl.total_ltv,
           SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date - cl.initial_purchase_date <= INTERVAL '7 days' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) as ltv_7day
    FROM customer_ltv cl
    JOIN payment p ON cl.customer_id = p.customer_id
    GROUP BY cl.customer_id, cl.initial_purchase_date, cl.total_ltv
),
customer_30day AS (
    SELECT cl.customer_id,
           cl.initial_purchase_date,
           cl.total_ltv,
           SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date - cl.initial_purchase_date <= INTERVAL '30 days' THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) as ltv_30day
    FROM customer_ltv cl
    JOIN payment p ON cl.customer_id = p.customer_id
    GROUP BY cl.customer_id, cl.initial_purchase_date, cl.total_ltv
)
SELECT 
    AVG(cltv.total_ltv) as avg_total_ltv,
    AVG(CASE WHEN cltv.total_ltv > 0 THEN (cltv_7d.ltv_7day * 1.0 / cltv.total_ltv) * 100 ELSE NULL END) as avg_pct_7day,

FROM customer_ltv cltv
JOIN customer_7day cltv_7d ON cltv.customer_id = cltv_7d.customer_id
JOIN customer_30day cltv_30d ON cltv.customer_id = cltv_30d.customer_id

WITH film_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        i.film_id,
        SUM(p.amount) as film_revenue
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
    JOIN payment p ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
    GROUP BY i.film_id
),
actor_film_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        fa.actor_id,
        fa.film_id,
        fr.film_revenue,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film_actor fa2 WHERE fa2.film_id = fa.film_id) as num_actors
    FROM film_actor fa
    JOIN film_revenue fr ON fa.film_id = fr.film_id
),
actor_top3 AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        film_id,
        film_revenue,
        num_actors,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY actor_id ORDER BY film_revenue DESC) as film_rank
    FROM actor_film_revenue
),
actor_top3_with_per_actor_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        film_id,
        film_revenue,
        num_actors,
        film_rank,
        film_revenue / num_actors as revenue_per_actor_in_film
    FROM actor_top3
    WHERE film_rank <= 3
),
actor_top3_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        SUM(revenue_per_actor_in_film) as avg_revenue_per_actor_in_top3_films
    FROM actor_top3_with_per_actor_revenue
    GROUP BY actor_id
)

    t.film_id,

FROM actor_top3_with_per_actor_revenue t

candidates.sql:
WITH film_revenue AS (
    SELECT film_id, SUM(amount) as total_revenue
    FROM payment
    JOIN rental ON payment.rental_id = rental.rental_id
    JOIN inventory ON rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id
    GROUP BY film_id
),
film_actor_count AS (
    SELECT film_id, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_id) as actor_count_in_film
    FROM film_actor
    GROUP BY film_id
),
actor_film_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        a.actor_id,
        a.first_name,
        a.last_name,
        f.film_id,
        f.title,
        fr.total_revenue,
        fac.actor_count_in_film,
        fr.total_revenue / fac.actor_count_in_film as revenue_per_actor
    FROM actor a
    JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
    JOIN film f ON fa.film_id = f.film_id
    JOIN film_revenue fr ON f.film_id = fr.film_id
    JOIN film_actor_count fac ON f.film_id = fac.film_id
),
ranked_films AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        film_id,
        title,
        total_revenue,
        actor_count_in_film,
        revenue_per_actor,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY actor_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC) as revenue_rank
    FROM actor_film_revenue
),
avg_per_actor AS (
    SELECT 
        actor_id,
        first_name,
        last_name,
        AVG(revenue_per_actor) as avg_rev
    FROM ranked_films
    WHERE revenue_rank <= 3
    GROUP BY actor_id, first_name, last_name
)
SELECT 
    rf.actor_id,
    rf.first_name,
    rf.last_name,
    rf.film_id,
    rf.title,
    rf.total_revenue,
    rf.actor_count_in_film,
    rf.revenue_per_actor,
    avg_per_actor.avg_rev
FROM ranked_films rf
JOIN avg_per_actor ON rf.actor_id = avg_per_actor.actor_id
WHERE rf.revenue_rank <= 3
ORDER BY rf.actor_id, rf.revenue_rank

WITH first_payment AS (
    SELECT customer_id, payment_id, rental_id
    FROM (
        SELECT customer_id, payment_id, rental_id,

        FROM payment

),

    FROM first_payment fp
),
first_film AS (
    SELECT fr.customer_id, fr.rental_id, r.inventory_id, i.film_id
    FROM first_rental fr
    JOIN rental r ON fr.rental_id = r.rental_id
    JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
),
first_rating AS (
    SELECT ff.customer_id, ff.film_id, f.rating
    FROM first_film ff
    JOIN film f ON ff.film_id = f.film_id
),
customer_amount AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, SUM(p.amount) as total_amount
    FROM customer c
    JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
customer_rentals AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id) as total_rentals
    FROM customer c
    LEFT JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
)

    AVG(ca.total_amount) as avg_total_amount,
    AVG(cr.total_rentals - 1) as avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM first_rating fr
JOIN customer_amount ca ON fr.customer_id = ca.customer_id
JOIN customer_rentals cr ON fr.customer_id = cr.customer_id
GROUP BY fr.rating
ORDER BY fr.rating

SELECT 
    fm.rating,
    AVG(p.total_amount) as avg_total_amount,
    AVG(CAST(r.total_rentals AS DOUBLE) - 1) as avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM (
    SELECT 
        p.customer_id,
        SUM(p.amount) as total_amount
    FROM payment p
    GROUP BY p.customer_id
) p
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT 
        r.customer_id,
        COUNT(*) as total_rentals
    FROM rental r
    GROUP BY r.customer_id
) r ON p.customer_id = r.customer_id
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT 
        p.customer_id,
        p.payment_id,
        r.inventory_id,
        i.film_id,
        f.rating
    FROM payment p
    INNER JOIN (
        SELECT customer_id, MIN(payment_date) as first_payment_date
        FROM payment
        GROUP BY customer_id
    ) fp ON p.customer_id = fp.customer_id AND p.payment_date = fp.first_payment_date
    INNER JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
    INNER JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    INNER JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
) fm ON p.customer_id = fm.customer_id
GROUP BY fm.rating
ORDER BY fm.rating

local197.question: Among our top 10 paying customers, can you identify the largest change in payment amounts from one month to the immediately following month? Specifically, please determine for which customer and during which month this maximum month-over-month difference occurred, and provide the difference rounded to two decimal places.

candidates.sql:
WITH top10 AS (
    SELECT customer_id
    FROM (
        SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) as total_amount
        FROM payment
        GROUP BY customer_id
        ORDER BY total_amount DESC
        LIMIT 10
    )
),
monthly_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        p.customer_id,
        strftime('%Y-%m', p.payment_date) as payment_month,
        SUM(p.amount) as monthly_total
    FROM payment p
    WHERE p.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM top10)
    GROUP BY p.customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', p.payment_date)
),
with_diff AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        payment_month,
        monthly_total,
        monthly_total - LAG(monthly_total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_month) as month_diff
    FROM monthly_totals
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    payment_month,
    ROUND(month_diff, 2) as max_diff
FROM with_diff 
WHERE month_diff IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY month_diff DESC
LIMIT 1

WITH stack_scores AS (

    FROM model_score

non_stack_max AS (

    FROM model_score

condition_rows AS (
    SELECT s.name, s.version, s.step

candidates.sql:
WITH stack_scores AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, test_score as stack_test_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model = 'Stack'
),
non_stack_max AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, MAX(test_score) as max_non_stack_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model != 'Stack'
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
problem_condition AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT sc.name
    FROM stack_scores sc
    JOIN non_stack_max ns ON sc.name = ns.name AND sc.version = ns.version AND sc.step = ns.step
    WHERE ns.max_non_stack_score < sc.stack_test_score
),
problem_counts AS (
    SELECT name, COUNT(*) as count
    FROM solution
    GROUP BY name
)
SELECT pc2.name, pc2.count
FROM problem_condition pc
JOIN problem_counts pc2 ON pc.name = pc2.name
WHERE pc2.count > 3
ORDER BY pc2.name

candidates.sql:
WITH 
stack_scores AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, test_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model = 'Stack'
),
non_stack_max AS (
    SELECT 
        name, version, step,
        MAX(test_score) as max_non_stack_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model != 'Stack'
    GROUP BY name, version, step
)
SELECT s.name, s.version, s.step, n.max_non_stack_score, s.test_score
FROM stack_scores s
JOIN non_stack_max n ON s.name = n.name AND s.version = n.version AND s.step = n.step
WHERE n.max_non_stack_score < s.test_score
LIMIT 30

local263.question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.

candidates.sql:
WITH step_scores AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, test_score as stack_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model = 'Stack'
),
non_stack_max AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, MAX(test_score) as max_non_stack
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model != 'Stack'
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
status_per_step AS (
    SELECT 
        n.name, 
        n.version, 
        n.step,
        CASE 
            WHEN n.max_non_stack < s.stack_score THEN 'strong'
            WHEN n.max_non_stack = s.stack_score THEN 'soft'
            ELSE 'neither'
        END as status
    FROM non_stack_max n
    JOIN step_scores s ON n.name = s.name AND n.version = s.version AND n.step = s.step
),
model_has_status AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT name, version, status
    FROM status_per_step
    WHERE status IN ('strong', 'soft')
),
l1_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        mhs.status,
        m.L1_model,
        COUNT(*) as count
    FROM model_has_status mhs
    JOIN model m ON mhs.name = m.name AND mhs.version = m.version
    GROUP BY mhs.status, m.L1_model
)
SELECT status, L1_model, count
FROM l1_counts
ORDER BY status, count DESC

candidates.sql:
WITH step_scores AS (
    SELECT ms.name, ms.version, ms.step,
           MAX(CASE WHEN ms.model != 'Stack' THEN ms.test_score END) as max_non_stack,
           MAX(CASE WHEN ms.model = 'Stack' THEN ms.test_score END) as stack_score
    FROM model_score ms
    JOIN model m ON ms.name = m.name AND ms.version = m.version AND ms.step = m.step
    GROUP BY ms.name, ms.version, ms.step
),
status_per_model AS (
    SELECT name, version,
           CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN max_non_stack < stack_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 'strong'
                WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN max_non_stack = stack_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 'soft'
                ELSE NULL END as status
    FROM step_scores
    GROUP BY name, version
),
model_with_status AS (
    SELECT s.name, s.version, s.status, m.L1_model
    FROM status_per_model s
    JOIN model m ON s.name = m.name AND s.version = m.version
    WHERE s.status IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT name, version, status, L1_model, COUNT(*) as cnt
FROM (
    SELECT * FROM model_with_status
)
GROUP BY name, version, status, L1_model

candidates.sql:
WITH step_comparison AS (
    SELECT name, version, step,
           MAX(CASE WHEN model = 'Stack' THEN test_score ELSE 0 END) as stack_score,
           MAX(CASE WHEN model != 'Stack' THEN test_score ELSE 0 END) as max_non_stack
    FROM model_score
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
model_status AS (
    SELECT name, version,
           MAX(CASE WHEN stack_score > max_non_stack THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as is_strong,
           MAX(CASE WHEN stack_score = max_non_stack THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as is_soft_candidate
    FROM step_comparison
    GROUP BY name, version
),
model_l1 AS (
    SELECT name, version, L1_model
    FROM model
    GROUP BY name, version, L1_model
),
model_with_status AS (
    SELECT ms.name, ms.version, ms.is_strong, ms.is_soft_candidate, m.L1_model
    FROM model_status ms
    JOIN model_l1 m ON ms.name = m.name AND ms.version = m.version
),
status_l1_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        CASE WHEN is_strong = 1 THEN 'strong' WHEN is_soft_candidate = 1 THEN 'soft' ELSE NULL END as status,
        L1_model,
        COUNT(*) as count
    FROM model_with_status
    WHERE is_strong = 1 OR is_soft_candidate = 1
    GROUP BY status, L1_model
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT status, L1_model, count,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY count DESC) as rn
    FROM status_l1_counts
)
SELECT status, L1_model, count
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY status

candidates.sql:
WITH step_max_nonstack AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, MAX(test_score) as max_nonstack
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model != 'Stack'
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
stack_scores AS (
    SELECT name, version, step, test_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE model = 'Stack'
),
status_calc AS (
    SELECT 
        s.name, s.version,
        MAX(CASE WHEN mns.max_nonstack < s.test_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as is_strong,
        MAX(CASE WHEN mns.max_nonstack = s.test_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as is_soft
    FROM stack_scores s
    LEFT JOIN step_max_nonstack mns ON s.name = mns.name AND s.version = mns.version AND s.step = mns.step
    GROUP BY s.name, s.version
),
model_l1 AS (
    SELECT name, version, L1_model FROM model
),
model_status AS (
    SELECT 
        ml.name, ml.version, ml.L1_model,
        sc.is_strong, sc.is_soft
    FROM model_l1 ml
    JOIN status_calc sc ON ml.name = sc.name AND ml.version = sc.version
)
SELECT 'strong' as status, L1_model, COUNT(*) as count
FROM model_status
WHERE is_strong = 1
GROUP BY L1_model
ORDER BY count DESC
